candidate_attempts.reason: Capability-matched HistGradientBoosting reaches pooled Brier skill 0.713 vs marginal reference (>0.70 agent ceiling); relative to the obvious situation prior (kind x outs x batted-ball type, skill 0.633) remaining headroom is only ~0.16 so scores would be saturated or compressed. Source access, Retrosheet notice license and coarse-tuple lookup non-uniqueness (5.98% unique) were fine; the core formulation fails the toy-baseline/headroom gate.

Two measured gate failures. (1) Lookup: the public artifact is a transformed copy of a public corpus image and MIRFLICKR publishes per-image EXIF text files containing ISO/Exposure/Aperture/Flash, i.e. every scored target; a crude 64-bit dHash on an 88pct crop + 512px resize + q85 re-encode still recovers the source id top-1 in 46/100 probes (median Hamming 15 to true source vs 32 to a random image), so a capable retrieval solver recovers answers outright and the only mitigation would destroy the noise/blur evidence the task depends on. (2) Capability gap: on 1849 photos / 860 photographers with photographer-grouped split, ResNet18+hand-feature GBM scored 0.303/0.178/0.309 credit for ISO/shutter/aperture vs train-median priors 0.294/0.149/0.287, and flash 0.9175 vs 0.9154 majority - essentially null skill at the redistributable 500px resolution, which would compress agent scores at the sample floor. Wikimedia Commons full-resolution alternative is unusable: HTTP 429 rate limiting for this egress IP even at one API call per 20s (146 photos harvested).
